patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: The pain started near my belly button, then packed up and moved down to the right like it had a GPS. I already threw up my ramen. Please do not make me laugh; it makes the pain worse.
presentation.triageNote: 19-year-old man with pain that began near the navel and migrated to the right lower quadrant over the day. He has nausea, vomiting, guarding, pain with movement or laughter, and a temperature of 37.8°C.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 3 is appropriate because the patient is stable and is expected to require more than one resource.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This is a stable abdominal-pain presentation that is expected to require multiple resources for laboratory assessment, imaging, symptom control, and possible surgical evaluation.
clinical.acuityReason: Migratory right-lower-quadrant pain, vomiting, guarding, and a low-grade fever require timely evaluation, but the patient has stable vital signs and no presented evidence of shock, severe systemic illness, or current need for a lifesaving intervention.
expectedResources: IV fluids, analgesia, and antiemetic medication
keyFindings: Pain began near the navel and migrated to the right lower quadrant
Pain worsened by movement or laughter
Stable blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygenation
teachingPoints: A stable patient may still need laboratory testing, imaging, medication, and specialty evaluation.
Triage reflects current acuity and anticipated care, not whether a particular abdominal diagnosis seems likely.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: The patient would remain NPO while receiving laboratory testing, abdominal imaging, fluids, and symptom control, with surgical treatment if imaging confirms an operative condition.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.pose: sitting hunched, both hands guarding the lower-right belly
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a Black 19-year-old college guy in a hoodie, on the same blue clinic chair. Pose: sitting hunched, both hands guarding the lower-right belly. Expression: tense grimace, holding very still. Clearly visible: hands protecting the right-lower abdomen, slightly sweaty. Overall genuinely uncomfortable but stable. No text, no logos.
